result.strongest_objection: The premise that 'Dwarfs top out at 10.7 kK... and are unaffected' by the 10^6 K Doppler LUT ceiling is unverified. There is no Verification Log row proving that the existing dwarf relations (teffFromBpRp) clamp at 10.7 kK or that the GCNS dwarf sample tops out there. If the existing relation covers hotter main-sequence stars (e.g., B-type dwarfs > 22.3 kK), they will also exceed the ceiling at 0.999c.
result.catch: Unverified factual claim about the maximum temperature of dwarfs in the existing pipeline or dataset.
result.proposed_fix: Add a Verification Log row (e.g., C4) proving the 10.7 kK maximum for dwarfs by either checking the teffFromBpRp bounds in photometry.ail or measuring the maximum non-WD temperature in the GCNS extract. If dwarfs can actually exceed 22.3 kK, update the 'Temperature consumers' section to include them in the 0.999c saturation impact analysis.

result.strongest_objection: PREMISE VERIFICATION failure on the WD-3 consumer contract: the doc's own evidence rule ('every premise has a row in the Verification log') is broken for two load-bearing claims. (1) The flags contract `flags = 1 (WD) | 4 (APPROX_TEFF) | 16 (TEFF_CLAMPED)` hard-codes bit assignments with no verification row: nothing cites the M1 doc or sprint lines that define the existing flags word — that bit 1 is WD, that bit 4 is APPROX_TEFF (as opposed to some other dwarf approximation flag), and critically that bit 16 is unallocated. The doc even extends bit 16 to dwarf rows where `bpRpInTable` is false, changing existing dwarf-row semantics; a collision or mis-assignment here silently corrupts the flag semantics of the production `checkWDRow` transform this milestone exists to unblock, and AC-W10's grep cannot catch it. This is exactly the class of premise that rows G3 (`grep -n wd tools/extract.py`) and K3 (grep for '0.3.0') demonstrate is cheap to verify, yet it was asserted. (2) The 'committed fixture WD row (BP−RP 1.0401, G 20.654)' from which the pinned checkWDPackage values (teff 5202.556030832587, v 20.899202194346880) are derived has no verification row either — N1 covers the parser's non-finite handling and test lines :18/:23, but never shows the fixture row exists with that photometry. If the fixture differs, the WD-3 pin values are wrong and the 'load-bearing pin in make test' fails or, worse, gets silently recomputed to fit.
